---
title: "Module 1: About This Computer"
subtitle: "About 15 hours · For teachers"
---

**The big idea:** students ask the computer about itself. They start with one line of Python that prints the processor type and build up to a labelled report stored in variables. Along the way they learn to read, predict, and trace code, use a module's tools, and read error messages. They also discover that a program reports on whatever computer it actually runs on.

**Expectations:** A1.1, A2.1, A2.2, A3.1, A4.2, A4.3, A4.4, C1.1, C1.4, C2.1, C3.1, C3.3, C3.4, C3.5 (across the whole module)

## Assignment

[**Computer Report Card**](assignment.qmd) (ready for Lessons 1–2; will grow with the module). Students read and trace a short program, write a report card using five `platform` functions stored in variables, then run it in two places and explain the difference. Students hand in one `.py` file built from a starter file.

**Planned additions:** an f-string version of the report, a short `input()` greeting, and a written part explaining what happens inside the computer when the report runs (RAM, CPU, interpreter).

**Adds to the toolkit:** `report_card.py`, the first file in the student's **My Computer Toolkit** folder, which grows in every module ([see the toolkit thread](../../scope-and-sequence.qmd#the-toolkit-thread)).

## Practising the Basics (Planned)

- **Skill Builder:** short drills on `print()` arguments, `sep` and `end`, escape characters, quotes, variables, types, f-strings, and reading a traceback. Each drill set opens with predict-the-output and fix-the-error questions.
- **Quick Builds** (small graded programs; each is the Make product of a lesson, so it needs no extra period):
  - [**System Banner**](quick-build-system-banner.qmd) (Lesson 3): a boxed title banner for the computer, with exact spacing.
  - [**Parts Receipt**](quick-build-parts-receipt.qmd) (Lesson 5): a receipt for computer parts, with prices, HST, and a total in aligned columns.

Until the Skill Builder is ready, use the [Practice](practice.qmd) page and the exit tickets for retrieval practice.

## How Module 1 Fits

- **Before:** nothing. This is the first module; students need no programming experience.
- **Planned for the rest of the module:** see Planned lessons above, and the [Scope and Sequence](../../scope-and-sequence.qmd).
- **Next:** [Module 2, Spec Checker](../module-02-spec-checker/index.qmd), adds `os` and `shutil` to check whether a computer meets a program's requirements.
- **Students set up first:** their [course folder](../../course-folder.qmd), before Lesson 1's Make.

New to the course? Read [How a Lesson Works](../../how-a-lesson-works.qmd) first.
